subsystems.name: Living structural material
subsystems.role: the bulk of the building: a mineralised composite that can be grown, cast or printed rather than quarried.

subsystems.name: Healing payload
subsystems.role: dormant organisms that wake when a crack lets in water and seal it.
parts: encapsulated spores in lightweight aggregate or hydrogel

subsystems.name: Vascular network
subsystems.role: channels that carry water, nutrients and healing agents to where damage occurs, the way a tree feeds its outer growth.

subsystems.name: Growth feedstock and forming
subsystems.role: the raw material and the mould or scaffold that shapes it.

subsystems.name: Sensing and control
subsystems.role: detects strain, moisture and cracks, and decides when to feed the material.
parts: embedded fibre-optic or piezoelectric strain sensors

subsystems.name: Carbon and nutrient cycling
subsystems.role: captures carbon in mineral form and keeps nutrients circulating through the district.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the organisms
buildSteps.detail: Select or modify spore-forming bacteria that precipitate calcite, and fungal strains that bind waste biomass into a stiff composite. They must survive high pH, heat and drying.

buildSteps.title: Protect the spores
buildSteps.detail: Encapsulate spores with a calcium and carbon nutrient source inside lightweight aggregate or gel capsules, so they survive mixing and stay dormant until a crack admits water.

buildSteps.title: Grow or cast the elements
buildSteps.detail: Mycelium is inoculated into packed waste substrate inside a mould and left for days to bind it; biocement is cast like concrete, with bacteria already embedded.

buildSteps.title: Build in the vasculature
buildSteps.detail: Channels or tubing are cast or printed through each element, connecting to ports where water and nutrients can be injected.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and seal joints
buildSteps.detail: Grown panels and cast elements are lifted into place, with joints designed to self-seal when wetted.

buildSteps.title: Wake the material
buildSteps.detail: A first wetting and feeding cycle triggers germination and mineral precipitation, filling pores and hairline cracks up to about a millimetre wide.

buildSteps.title: Instrument and commission
buildSteps.detail: Sensors report strain, moisture and pH to a control system that schedules feeding and flags damage.

buildSteps.title: Operate the building as a living system
buildSteps.detail: Nutrients are dosed periodically, carbon is locked into mineral phases, and worn elements are composted or regrown rather than landfilled.

prerequisites.why: calcite-precipitating bacteria have sealed cracks in laboratory and field trials since the 2010s, but the material is not yet standard for structural use.
mycelium panels and packaging are made commercially, yet load-bearing structural grades are still research.
strains must be engineered to work in concrete's alkaline, dry, nutrient-poor conditions without escaping control.
a living building only heals on demand if damage and moisture can be sensed reliably and cheaply.
growing building-sized elements needs controlled facilities with consistent temperature, humidity and sterility.

pathway.milestone: self-healing admixtures and bacterial treatments in niche repairs
pathway.unlocks: field data on how long healing lasts and how much it costs.

pathway.milestone: standardised biocement and mycelium elements for non-structural uses
pathway.unlocks: volume production, codes and measured carbon storage in mineral form.

pathway.milestone: load-bearing grown elements with vascular feeding and sensors in demonstration buildings
pathway.unlocks: proof that a structure can be maintained biologically over decades.

pathway.milestone: districts with nutrient supply and biorepair services
pathway.unlocks: urban fabric that accrues mineral carbon, self-seals minor damage and is regrown rather than demolished.
